intro.title: Service Overview
intro.body: iGM CLI is a command-line download tool built jointly by iGCraftLit × MuoCeon. It lets you search, download, update, and uninstall resources from iGCraftLit Community directly in CMD, PowerShell, or Bash, with first-class support for Minecraft mods, resource packs, maps, and modpacks. Every command uses the igm prefix.

features.title: Features
items: Search, download, and install with a single command.
Filter by game version and loader, including Forge, Fabric, NeoForge, and Quilt.
The igm.json config file supports batch installation and team collaboration.
Resumable downloads, local cache, and hash verification.
Integrated with the iGCraftLit account system, with login and synced download history.

eligibility.title: Eligibility
items: Public resources can be downloaded without signing in.
For private or login-required resources, run igm login first.
Access is fully open during the early stage and will be tightened gradually based on usage patterns.
Users must comply with the iGCraftLit Community User Rules.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.hint: Below is an overview of frequently asked questions. See the FAQ page for full answers.
faq.q1: Why is my request being rate limited?
faq.a1: To keep the service stable, the API enforces rate limits per IP address and per account. Very frequent requests are throttled temporarily; please wait and retry. Signing in grants a higher quota. If the problem persists, run igm doctor to check your network and backend connectivity.
faq.a2: When signed in, search and download history is synced with your account so you can view it across devices. When signed out, only the local cache is kept, which you can clear at any time with igm cache clean. We never collect terminal session content without authorization.
faq.a3: The iGM CLI tool itself is free and may be used for resource management in commercial environments. Resources downloaded through the tool remain subject to their own open-source licenses and author terms. Verify each resource's license before commercial use and follow the iGCraftLit Community User Rules.
faq.q4: How do I report an issue?
faq.a4: Email the team at igcraftlit@outlook.com (.NET) or igcraftlit@163.com (.CN), or submit feedback at https://igcraftlit.com. Putting "iGM CLI" in the subject line helps us locate the issue faster.

overview.title: Adapter Overview
overview.body: The adapter is the bridge between a launcher and the iGM download engine. Through the adapter protocol or the SDK, a launcher hands resource download requests to the iGM engine, which performs requesting, transfer, verification, and disk writing in the background, and reports progress back to the launcher through an event stream. No terminal window pops up and the user interface is never interrupted.

compare.title: Integration Options
compare.lead: Launchers can choose between two integration options: SDK embedding and the adapter protocol. Pick based on your language stack and delivery model.

options.name: SDK embedding
options.langs: C, C++, Zig, Rust, Go, and other languages with C ABI support
pros: No extra process; best performance; naturally terminal-free
Links the engine directly for the shortest call path
cons: A platform-specific dynamic library build is required per platform

options.name: Adapter protocol
options.langs: Any language that can send HTTP requests
pros: Cross-language and cross-platform with no embedded code
The service can be upgraded independently without rebuilding the launcher
cons: A local resident service is required; networking and connections must be handled

protocol.title: Adapter Protocol (HTTP + WebSocket)
protocol.lead: The adapter protocol uses REST + WebSocket, and all endpoints share a common prefix:

create.title: Create a download task
create.desc: Submit the resource identifier, version, loader, and target directory. On success, a task ID is returned for later queries and subscriptions.

query.title: Query task progress
query.desc: Poll a task ID for the current status, downloaded bytes, total bytes, percentage, speed, and estimated remaining seconds.

ws.title: Real-time progress push
ws.desc: Once the WebSocket connection is established, the server continuously pushes progress events for the task without polling.

cancel.title: Cancel a task
cancel.desc: Tell the engine to abort the transfer and clean up temporary chunks; the task then moves to the cancelled state.

events.lead: All progress events share one unified structure, returned by both the WebSocket push and the task query endpoint:

terminal.title: Running Without a Terminal Window
items: SDK embedding: the library runs inside the launcher process, so there is naturally no terminal.
Adapter protocol: the local service must hide its window using platform APIs.
terminal.unix: Linux / macOS: use fork + setsid without allocating a TTY.
terminal.forbid: Never call system, popen, or exec to run the CLI — a terminal window will always appear.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.hint: Below is an overview of common adapter integration questions. Full answers are provided on this page.
faq.a1: Public resources can be downloaded without sign-in. For private resources or synced download history, include an iGCraftLit account token in the request; the token uses the same account system as igm login.
faq.q2: Which languages does the SDK support?
faq.a2: The SDK is based on the C ABI and works with any language that can link a dynamic library, including C, C++, Zig, Rust, and Go. Languages without C ABI support should use the HTTP + WebSocket adapter protocol instead.
faq.q3: Does the adapter protocol support resumable downloads?
faq.a3: Yes. After an interruption, query the task status with the task ID and continue the task. The engine skips chunks that have already passed hash verification and emits retry events on automatic retries.
faq.q4: How do I report an adapter issue?
faq.a4: Email the team at igcraftlit@outlook.com (.NET) or igcraftlit@163.com (.CN), or submit feedback at https://igcraftlit.com. Putting "Adapter" in the subject line helps us locate the issue faster.
